references.text: Moses becomes angry and throws the tablets from him. This shows Moses' characteristic reaction of anger when the people of Israel sin or stray from God's commands.
Moses becomes angry at Aaron's sons. Another example of Moses' anger directed toward leaders who did not follow God's instructions exactly.
The commanders, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds are mentioned again later in the same chapter, showing the military structure in Israel.
The organizational structure with leaders over thousands and leaders over hundreds was established on Jethro's advice to Moses.
Moses recalls the appointment of captains of thousands and captains of hundreds as leaders for the tribes.
The context of the war against the Midianites from which these commanders returned.
Simeon and Levi killed all the men after the incident at Shechem, but Jacob was displeased. In contrast, Moses is angry here because not all enemies were killed.
